source: NCERT Class X, Contemporary India II, Geography Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. Water Scarcity and Its Causes
points: **Freshwater** is only a tiny fraction (about 2.5%) of the total water on Earth; most is in ice sheets and glaciers.
**Water scarcity** may exist even in areas of adequate rainfall due to **over-exploitation, over-use and unequal access**.
Causes: growing population (more water for food, industry, cities), over-irrigation, industrialisation, urbanisation, and pollution of rivers by sewage and industrial effluents.

sections.heading: 2. Multi-Purpose River Projects and Dams
points: **Dams** are built for irrigation, electricity (hydel power), water supply, flood control, recreation, inland navigation and fish breeding — hence **multi-purpose projects**.
**Jawaharlal Nehru** called dams the **'temples of modern India'**.
Examples: **Bhakra-Nangal (Sutlej), Hirakud (Mahanadi), Nagarjuna Sagar, Tehri, Sardar Sarovar (Narmada), Damodar Valley**.

sections.heading: 3. Problems and Opposition to Dams
points: Dams cause **submergence of land and forests, displacement of local people**, loss of livelihoods and biodiversity.
They can induce **sedimentation** in reservoirs, and worsen floods when sediment is not flushed.
**Movements** against big dams: **Narmada Bachao Andolan** (Sardar Sarovar) and **Tehri Dam** protests — over rehabilitation and ecology.
Inter-state disputes over water sharing (e.g. Krishna, Cauvery).

sections.heading: 4. Rainwater Harvesting — Traditional and Modern
points: **Rainwater harvesting** conserves water and recharges groundwater; a low-cost, sustainable alternative.

Traditional systems: **'guls'/'kuls'** (Himalayas), **'khadins'/'johads'** and **tankas** (Rajasthan), **rooftop harvesting** (Shillong, Meghalaya), **bamboo drip irrigation** (Meghalaya), **inundation channels** (Bengal).
In **Rajasthan (Bikaner, Phalodi, Barmer)**, underground tanks (tankas) store rainwater for drinking.
In **Gendathur (Karnataka)** and many regions, rooftop rainwater harvesting is common; some states made it **mandatory**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Nehru = dams are 'temples of modern India'.
Bhakra-Nangal (Sutlej), Hirakud (Mahanadi), Sardar Sarovar (Narmada), Damodar Valley.
Narmada Bachao Andolan = against Sardar Sarovar dam.
Tankas/khadins = Rajasthan; guls/kuls = Himalayas; bamboo drip irrigation = Meghalaya.
Rooftop rainwater harvesting = Shillong, Gendathur (Karnataka).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Bhakra-Nangal** is on the **Sutlej**; **Hirakud** on the **Mahanadi**; **Sardar Sarovar** on the **Narmada**.
**Narmada Bachao Andolan** opposed the **Sardar Sarovar** dam.
**Bamboo drip irrigation** is a traditional method of **Meghalaya**.
Dams are **multi-purpose** (not only for electricity).
